content.text:
I submitted **index 29 (Mg 0.19 / Sb 0.81)** as the best composition. All three merit measurements are used, but EQE was very low everywhere I measured, so the best result is still weak.

| Index | Mg / Sb | Why I measured it | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 24 | 0.34 / 0.66 | MgSb2O6: stable, predicted gap 2.8 eV, closest to the 2.7 eV light | 0.0007 |
| **29** | **0.19 / 0.81** | Sb-rich phases have predicted gaps small enough to absorb the light | **0.0055** |
| 18 | 0.51 / 0.49 | 1:1 region, predicted gap 1.2 eV, not yet sampled | 0.00015 |

- **Why index 29:** its EQE was about 8× index 24 and about 37× index 18. Its X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern shows extra peaks that index 24's doesn't, which suggests additional Sb-rich oxide phases. I didn't confirm this: the XRD match against known phases was poor (best similarity 0.13, for MgSb2O6).
- **Mg-rich end (indices 0–12) not measured:** the phases there are predicted to have band gaps of 3.1–4.2 eV, too wide to absorb 2.7 eV light.
- **Main gap:** I didn't measure the neighbours of index 29 (indices 25–28). If EQE keeps rising toward the Sb-rich end, 29 is likely the library's best, but that's untested.

I used 2 of the 5 XRD scans.
